neighbours.label: ',' / ' and' joining sequential physical actions in narrative or instructions (before the next action)
fire: Pull up a chair next to the expert, watch what she does and copy her.
Unwrap the chilled dough and roll it out on the parchment.
When she reached the tree, she saw the hole and knelt beside it.
He opened the chest, took out the map and spread it on the table.
She dried her hands, picked up the phone and dialed the number.
The dog dug up the bone, carried it to the porch and dropped it.
Heat the pan, add the onions and stir until they soften.
He climbed the stairs, knocked twice and waited for an answer.
quiet: The expert next to the window is tall, quiet and very patient.
The chilled dough is soft, sticky and slightly sweet.
The tree near the house is old, tall and full of birds.
The chest held old maps, coins and letters from the war.
Her hands were cold, red and covered in flour.
The dog is brown, friendly and a little lazy.
The pan is heavy, black and made of cast iron.
The stairs were narrow, steep and badly lit.
